MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan has ordered the three-month preventive suspension of a Pasay City regional judge who is facing a direct bribery charge filed in August by the Office of the Ombudsman.

The Sandiganbayan’s 6th Division rejected Pasay Regional Trial Court Branch 108 Judge Albert Cansino’s opposition, citing Section 13 of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, which makes preventive suspension mandatory for public officials facing a valid charge under the law involving fraud against the government or public funds or property.
Cansino was charged together with court interpreter Mariejoy Lagman over the alleged solicitation and receipt, directly or indirectly, of P6 million from a litigant in a property dispute.

blocks.caption: Ombudsman Remulla: Corruption in judiciary also ‘severe’

blocks.text: The order was signed by associate justices Sarah Jane Fernandez, Kevin Narce Vivero and Lord Villanueva, and directed the Office of the Court Administrator to enforce the suspension.

The bribery case stemmed from the May 23, 2024 arrest of Lagman in an entrapment operation conducted by the National Bureau of Investigation. The operation followed an anonymous complaint sent to the Judicial Integrity Board.

NBI agents found during the arrest a copy of a May 15, 2024 order signed by Cansino. A certified true copy of the order had been received by a representative of the defendants in the Pasay court property dispute.
The P6 million was allegedly sought as a “consideration for a favorable decision” in the civil case.
Cansino argued against the Sandiganbayan’s authority to suspend him, arguing that only the Supreme Court had the power to discipline and suspend judges.
He said the SC had already placed him under preventive suspension for 90 days in 2024 over the same allegations, extending the measure twice for a total of nine months.
Cansino said he resumed his judicial duties in February 2025 “without issue, interference, or untoward incident.”
But the Sandiganbayan rejected the argument, saying the SC’s suspension was imposed in an administrative proceeding, while the case before it was criminal in nature.

“This Court must, however, emphasize that administrative proceedings are separate and distinct from criminal proceedings, even if the said proceedings arose from the same facts and circumstances,” the anti-graft court said. – Rappler.com
